newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO NAPHTHA PRICES STEADY, IGNORE CRUDE GAINS.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO NAPHTHA PRICES STEADY, IGNORE CRUDE GAINS.

text.p: Naphtha prices were barely changed in afternoon Tokyo trade on Thursday, shrugging off gains on overseas crude oil markets, which usually set direction for Asian naphtha, traders said.
"Today, Japan's naphtha almost completely ignored the crude rise," one trader said.
Naphtha's failure to follow the upward crude movement proved how weak the regional naphtha market was, he said.
Prompt cargoes for September delivery were especially weak with plenty of physical supplies amid almost no demand from petrochemical end-users, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha was notionally quoted at $206.00/$206.50 per tonne for first-half October delivery. It was traded several times at $206.00 on Wednesday.

In heavy fuel oil trading, Indonesian low sulphur waxy residue cargoes were sold to Japan at 80 to 90 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula earlier this week, wrapping up spot trading for August cargoes, traders said.
